clue.text: Royal couple eat perch caught by one of these, perhaps

definitions.text: Royal couple eat perch caught by one of these, perhaps

indicators.note: to eat something is to take it inside, so the royal pair wrap around the fish

parts.note: two royals: a king, and ER, the Latin initials of Queen Elizabeth (Elizabeth Regina)
two royals: a king, and ER, the Latin initials of Queen Elizabeth (Elizabeth Regina)
a perch is a freshwater fish

explanation.surface: A king and queen sit down to a perch supper, the fish having been caught by a bird.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Royal couple' gives two pieces, the king and the queen's ER cipher. The whole clue then doubles as the definition: a perch is just the sort of prey this diving bird catches.
explanation.definitionFit: This brightly coloured bird dives into rivers to catch small fish such as perch.

clue.text: One thousand and one cooking hobs to spoil

parts.note: K is the usual abbreviation for a thousand (kilo)
the Roman numeral I is one

indicators.note: something cooking is being worked on and changed, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A thousand and one hobs on the go in a kitchen, all ruining the meal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cooking' looks like a kitchen word, but it is the anagram signal: the four letters of 'hobs' are reshuffled to BOSH.
explanation.definitionFit: To put the kibosh on a plan is to put a stop to it; as a verb it means to ruin or scupper.

clue.text: Deny Lonsdale belts are something to wear

indicators.note: belts says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Someone denies that Lonsdale belts, boxing trophies, are an item of clothing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'belts' looks like part of the name Lonsdale belts (boxing championship prizes), but it is a verb meaning holds tight: deNY LONSdale holds the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Stockings made of a synthetic fibre are worn on the legs, so they are clothing.

clue.text: They certainly see lots of people!

definitions.text: They certainly see lots of people!

parts.words: They certainly see lots of people!
parts.note: reads as busy folk who meet many visitors, but lots means fates, and these people foresee the fates of their clients

explanation.definitionFit: Clairvoyants who predict what the future holds are said to see a person's lot or destiny.

clue.text: Asking her out might mean a loss of business!

indicators.note: out suggests the letters are in disarray, so they must be rearranged

explanation.surface: A man worries that inviting a woman on a date could cost him trade.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' looks like part of 'asking her out' for a date, but it is the anagram signal applied to ASKING HER.
explanation.definitionFit: In retail, stock lost to theft or waste reduces trade; a contraction or dwindling of anything.

clue.text: Regret never having returned to register

indicators.note: returned says the letters held in those words are read backwards
having means containing, so the words regret never hold the answer inside them

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Someone who came back to sign in has no regrets.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft gave no hidden-word signal; 'having' (holding) is it, and 'returned' turns the run RETNE, from regRET NEver, round.
explanation.definitionFit: To sign in or record one's name, as when one puts a horse in a race or a name on a list.

clue.text: Frank writer on love

indicators.note: in an across clue, one piece on another is written after it

parts.note: love is nil in tennis, written O
a pen is a writing instrument

explanation.surface: An outspoken author writes about love.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Frank' looks like a man's name, but it is the adjective meaning candid.
explanation.definitionFit: Being candid and honest is being plain-spoken, with nothing hidden.

clue.text: Locate smells and find remedies, possibly

parts.note: to locate something is to place or position it
BO is body odour, so BOS are smells

explanation.surface: A detective sniffs out where something is and turns up some cures.
explanation.walkthrough: BO stands for body odour; the plural gives BOS. 'possibly' is fair because these dummy pills only work through the patient's belief.
explanation.definitionFit: Inert pills given for their psychological effect act as cures only in the patient's mind.

clue.text: Points south — that's hardly necessary

parts.note: needles are sharp points

explanation.surface: A compass needle pointing south is a pointless thing to mention.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Points' looks like a verb, but it is a plural noun.
explanation.definitionFit: Something uncalled-for or superfluous is unnecessary.

clue.text: Trouble with drink? Take it to bed!

parts.note: to be in hot water is to be in trouble
the bottle stands for drink, as in being on the bottle or hitting the bottle

explanation.surface: Advice to someone whose drinking has caused problems: sleep it off.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is cryptic: a rubber container filled from the kettle is something one takes to bed on a cold night.
explanation.definitionFit: A rubber warmer filled from the kettle is tucked under the covers to heat the sheets.

clue.text: One makes bundles from the French in drinking establishment

indicators.note: in says the French word goes inside the drinking place

parts.note: a bar is a place for drinking
le is French for the

explanation.surface: A drinker in a bar makes a lot of money out of the French.
explanation.walkthrough: 'makes bundles' suggests making a fortune; it is a farm machine that bundles hay.
explanation.definitionFit: A farm machine that compresses hay or straw into tied blocks.

clue.text: Limit the amount of beer with this explanation

parts.note: to ration is to limit the amount allowed
ale is a kind of beer

explanation.surface: A landlord justifies cutting back on drinks.
explanation.definitionFit: The underlying reasoning or justification behind a decision.

clue.text: Put the heat on a tabloid newspaper and get exposure

indicators.note: in an across clue, one piece on another is written after it

parts.note: The Sun is a British tabloid daily
to burn something is to apply heat to it

explanation.surface: Pressure is put on a tabloid, which ends up in the public eye.
explanation.walkthrough: THE SUN is a British tabloid newspaper. 'exposure' suggests publicity, but here it means time spent unprotected under the sun.
explanation.definitionFit: Reddened skin is the result of too long in strong sunshine, the effect of exposure rather than its synonym.

clue.text: Fighting back, dish out unfair treatment

indicators.note: back says the word for fighting is read in reverse

parts.note: war is fighting
to deal is to hand out, as cards

explanation.surface: Someone who fights back gives others a hard time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fighting back' reads as resisting; 'back' is the reversal signal, giving RAW.
explanation.definitionFit: Being treated harshly or unjustly is getting a bad bargain.

clue.text: People grow old — or it's a change for this relationship!

parts.note: men are people
to age is to grow old

indicators.note: a change means the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: People get older, which is when a relationship might need shaking up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'change' reshuffles the letters of 'or it's a' into A TROIS, the French for 'with three'.
explanation.definitionFit: A French phrase for a household of three, where a couple share a lover.

clue.text: Reinvigorated on seeing red, perhaps

indicators.note: perhaps says these letters could be arranged another way

explanation.surface: Someone is fired up after losing their temper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'perhaps' rearranges SEEING RED.
explanation.definitionFit: Being given fresh vigour or vitality, revitalised.

clue.text: Believe to be under a cloud at first, but provide certification

indicators.note: in a down clue, a piece under another is written below it, so the word for believe goes after
at first takes the opening letter of the word cloud

parts.note: to credit something is to believe it

explanation.surface: To be under suspicion at first, then be officially approved.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Believe' gives CREDIT, which sits under A and C (the first letter of 'cloud').
explanation.definitionFit: To accredit someone is to officially recognise them as qualified, giving them credentials.

clue.text: Ignore note on girl with such an accent

indicators.note: in a down clue, one piece on another sits above it

parts.note: to cut someone is to snub or ignore them
G is a musical note
lass is a word for a girl

explanation.surface: Someone snubs a girl who speaks very posh.
explanation.walkthrough: A cut-glass accent is the clipped, precise speech of the English upper class.
explanation.definitionFit: Describes a very refined, upper-class English way of speaking, sharp and clear like crystal.

clue.text: Alec's beer cue became a notorious incident!

indicators.note: became says the letters turned into something else, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: Alec's drinking cue in a pub became a scandal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'became' rearranges ALEC'S BEER CUE.
explanation.definitionFit: A French phrase for a controversial case that attracts great public attention.

clue.text: Relax after a French victory over Germany

indicators.note: in a down clue, one piece over another sits above it

parts.note: un is French for a
a win is a victory
D is the international vehicle code for Germany

explanation.surface: Unwinding after France beats Germany at football.
explanation.walkthrough: D (Deutschland) is the international car code for Germany.
explanation.definitionFit: To unwind is to wind down or loosen up after tension.

clue.text: Rest the spinner

definitions.meaning: in snooker, a rest with raised legs lets the cue pass over other balls
an eight-legged creature that spins webs

explanation.definitionFit: Both a cue rest in snooker or billiards and a web-spinning arachnid.

clue.text: Even soldiers pull back in front of a river

indicators.note: in front of says these pieces come before what follows

parts.note: RE are the Royal Engineers, a regiment of soldiers

indicators.note: back says the word for pull is read in reverse

parts.note: to lug is to pull or drag

explanation.surface: Troops retreat ahead of a river, at a steady pace.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Even' looks like an adverb but is the adjective meaning steady; 'back' reverses the word for pull, giving GUL.
explanation.definitionFit: Regular in the sense of uniform or steady, as an even pace or rhythm.

clue.text: Spiritual leader who might talk endlessly

indicators.note: endlessly says the last letter is cut off

parts.note: rabbit means to chatter, from Cockney rhyming slang rabbit and pork for talk

explanation.surface: A religious leader who preaches at great length.
explanation.walkthrough: RABBIT means to chatter, from Cockney rhyming slang (rabbit and pork = talk); 'endlessly' removes its last letter, T.
explanation.definitionFit: A Jewish religious teacher and leader of a congregation.

clue.text: Confess to disheartened gaffer, being mature

indicators.note: to here means attached onto, so the word for confess is joined after the other piece
disheartened removes the heart, leaving only the outer letters of the word gaffer

parts.note: to own up is to confess

explanation.surface: An old boss with low spirits admits something, which is the adult thing to do.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gaffer' is British slang for a boss or an old man; with its heart removed it leaves G and R.
explanation.definitionFit: Being adult and fully developed.

clue.text: Verbal attacks when bride is at work

indicators.note: work means the letters are worked into a new order

explanation.surface: A bride at work gets an earful.
explanation.walkthrough: 'at work' reads as one phrase, but the 'at' is part of the letters rearranged: BRIDE IS AT.
explanation.definitionFit: Bitter spoken or written denunciations, tirades.

clue.text: Judged to be exhausted, having run back

indicators.note: back says that letter goes further back towards the start

parts.note: tired means exhausted
R is the cricket abbreviation for run

explanation.surface: Someone is deemed worn out after running back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' moves the R of TIRED one place towards the front.
explanation.definitionFit: Tried as in heard in court, a case being tried by a judge.

clue.text: Make an enquiry after tense undertaking

indicators.note: after says the word for enquiring comes behind the other piece

parts.note: T is the abbreviation for tense in grammar
to ask is to make an enquiry

explanation.surface: Someone asks a question after a nervous project.
explanation.definitionFit: A job or piece of work one takes on.

clue.text: Stage magician fills pit worker with fear

indicators.note: fills says the word for fear goes inside

parts.note: a miner works down a pit
dread is fear

explanation.surface: A stage magician terrifies a coal miner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fills ... with' reads as terrifying a miner; in fact the fear sits inside the pit worker.
explanation.definitionFit: A performer who claims to know what audience members are thinking.
